title: improv·artist · scientific (Tomás Saraceno)
mutation_directive: improv artist: scientific via Tomás Saraceno

improv_extras.practice: spider webs, cosmic networks; aerocene, balloons, ecological web

v1.feedback: Strong Saraceno read — the orb-web topology is immediately recognizable and the RK4 double-pendulum oscillator is a genuinely 'scientific' driver, not decorative math. Two improvements: the web is essentially flat (slight dome via -r²×0.009) so from this camera angle it reads as a 2D diagram rather than a tensioned 3D structure; tilt the camera ~15° below the plane or add a second web plane at an angle to give parallax depth. The 200 cosmic dust motes risk drifting into 'ambient nebula' territory — halve the count or confine them to the web plane so they read as dew/silk-caught light rather than generic space particles.

v2.feedback: Strong Saraceno translation — orb-weaver topology with double-pendulum hub tension is both biologically correct and conceptually apt (web as instrument responding to invisible forces). The restrained bone/ash palette on midnight reads as gallery-grade. Two refinements: the ghost reflection at 0.05 opacity is nearly invisible and costs geometry for little payoff — consider replacing it with a faint circular caustic projected below the hub (a single textured plane) to suggest the web catching light. Second, the background web2 group is static while the main web breathes; giving it a very slight independent drift (different pendulum phase) would reinforce Saraceno's cosmic-web parallax idea rather than feeling like a flat backdrop.
